candidates.rationale: Event accepts unrestricted strings. This is an injectivity defect in the reference example; production ledger equivalence or signature bypass was not established.

Append checks parent existence only; graph serialization consumes the ambiguous records.
graph_sha256 hashes exactly canonical_graph.

guards: Parent-existence assertion constrains DAG links, not string encoding.
Sorting parents and event IDs gives stable ordering but cannot disambiguate field boundaries.
No reference CLI or runtime was executed.

Static finding is confined to this example manifest field.

Timing under exceptional scheduling was not tested.

candidates.rationale: The documented unconditional Ring 0 exclusion is not enforced independently of configuration. with_config accepts RingPolicy without validation; membership in t3_allowed_rings plus Some(engine) is the entire eligibility predicate. A policy containing 0 with a short Tier 1 timeout reaches the Tier 2/Tier 3 race. The Ring 0 SystemHalt branch exists only within the opposite (!t3_allowed) branch. Tier 3 health/cooldown may still reject an unavailable engine. This proves a routing invariant gap, not a protected-effect authorization bypass.

source_checks.observation: Documentation says Ring 0 requests never reach Tier 3.

guards: Default policy [1,2,3] excludes Ring 0.

candidates.rationale: generate_scitt_receipt puts sig_ed25519_ plus 32 hexadecimal characters of a public payload digest in signature_ed25519. The complete function has no private key, signer, or signature operation. Both exposed tools return this receipt and pass it to append_auto_log, so the advertised signature authentication is absent on these paths. An adversary can recompute this field from public payload bytes; no downstream consumer accepting it as authorization was established.

candidates.rationale: SexaRegister.add uses unchecked u64 addition, while mul_scalar uses unchecked u128 multiplication then truncates the quotient with as u64. For example seconds=2^63 and factor=2 already produce a quotient of 2^64 that truncates to zero without needing u128 overflow. execute calls these helpers directly rather than returning an arithmetic error through poison_and_abort. Larger unchecked additions/products can wrap with overflow checks disabled or panic with them enabled; b60_run_bytecode has an extern C boundary and no panic catcher. Native panic/abort behavior was not executed, and no deployment build profile was assumed.

source_checks.observation: Unchecked additions/products and narrowing cast permit incorrect arithmetic or panic.
Normal fail-closed handling requires returning through poison_and_abort.
Add and multiply bypass Result-based arithmetic handling used by subtract/divide.
C ABI directly calls execute and handles Result only.

guards: Subtract underflow and exact division errors are checked, but do not cover add/multiply.
Public register fields also allow direct Rust callers to construct boundary values.
No Rust binary, FFI call, or overflow reproduction was executed.

candidates.rationale: Jump, JumpIfZero and JumpIfNotZero validate availability of encoded operands but never validate the decoded target. A taken jump beyond bytecode.len() sets pc beyond the loop boundary; the next loop check ends execution and returns Ok while manifest remains RUNNING and is_halted remains false. b60_run_bytecode converts that Ok to 0. This statically establishes acceptance of out-of-buffer control flow; no native VM run was performed.

source_checks.observation: Loop guard is pc < bytecode.len(); fuel limit is checked only inside the loop.
Jump branches check operand length only, then assign target to pc.
Unhandled opcodes poison; ordinary loop termination returns Ok.
FFI validates null/empty input and maps execute Ok to success code 0.

guards: Truncated jump operands and unknown opcodes are rejected.
Fuel cap prevents prolonged loops, not a target outside the bytecode buffer.
Conditional cases require their register predicate to be true.

candidates.rationale: Snapshot and manifest names contain only a UTC timestamp to the second. Two calls in that second select the same destination, with no exclusive name allocation, lock, or retry. The later manifest write is also nonexclusive. The name collision and unhandled collision path are statically confirmed; concurrent SQLite execution was not performed.

candidates.rationale: Every parent pipeline overwrites the fixed /tmp/c5_source_embeddings.npz, and every subprocess worker loads that same name. session_id is used for audio/video chunk paths but is not applied to embeddings or passed as an embeddings argument. Another pipeline can overwrite the identity data between the first parent write and worker loads. The one-worker branch passes src_faces in memory, so its own render does not load this shared file, although its parent write can interfere with another multiworker job. Actual media, identities and concurrency were not exercised.

guards: Per-session chunk filenames do not protect shared embeddings.

candidates.rationale: render_worker_chunk breaks on failed cap.read or a caught pipe write error, then discards the encoder wait status and has no expected-frame-count assertion. Parent subprocess checks only Python exit codes; successful concat/mux is checked, but a valid shorter chunk can satisfy those operations. Thus an early decode stop, or an encoder failure that leaves a parseable chunk and no exception during stdin.close, can reach DONE with fewer frames. Some pipe failures may still raise at close or produce an unreadable chunk caught by later check=True, so not every encoder failure is silent.

source_checks.observation: Worker reads a fixed frame budget but breaks immediately on decode failure.
Pipe write errors break the loop; wait return value is discarded.
Parent checks Python status and concat/mux success, without measuring frame completeness.
DONE is printed based on reaching the end, with FPS calculated from expected total_frames.

guards: Nonzero Python worker exits abort; concat/mux subprocesses use check=True.
Malformed/unreadable chunks may fail later, while a shorter valid chunk need not.
No FFmpeg, decoder, neural model, or media pipeline was launched.

candidates.rationale: forge_identity generates fresh seed material and uses touch(exist_ok=True) followed by open(...,w) on the existing master seed path. It neither rejects an existing identity nor writes via an atomic replacement with durability checks. The seal_bounty_aeon consumer calls it after any load exception, including decryption failures, so a wrong passphrase can lead to replacing the previous private identity instead of preserving it. An interrupted write can leave unreadable content. Loss of future signing capability with the original key is supported; historical signatures remain verifiable if their public key was separately retained. No actual seed or operator identity was accessed.

source_checks.observation: New random seed unconditionally replaces master_seed.enc through a truncating write.

candidates.rationale: The emitted validateTransition explicitly ignores currentSeq and enforces only write-state/parity constraints. The Rust generator supplies its own synthetic pattern rather than accepting arbitrary runtime traces; the confirmed issue is the stronger end-to-end causality claim made for this limited example verifier.
